## Part 2 — Interpretation

### Background

Parent #533's bare-word install-step grid found that a bare `pirate`/`villain` role header carries LESS wrong-persona marker mass than a content-matched minimal system prompt from install onward — but its apparent average-leakage advantage hid a probe split, and the comparison lived partly in a saturated regime where cross-arm log-p contrasts reduce to base-prior differences. This task re-read the parent's committed four-float logit captures with two cleaner measuring sticks: (a) the unsaturated checkpoints (s18 is the only point where both arms sit in/adjacent to the [5, 12]-nat usable band, at matched log-p implant strength, before any emission), and (b) the EOS-margin readout Δ(z_marker − z_eos), which is gauge-invariant and cannot be compressed by the softmax ceiling (valid here because LoRA excludes the unembedding — `gauge_assert.ok` on all 240 cells). Zero new training; the manipulated variable is the readout/regime. The plan's preview (computed during planning over these same files) pointed at the confirmed outcome; the production run re-derived everything from raw arrays with the verdict logic frozen in the plan — this is **disclosed preview-confirmation on the same draws**, not an independent replication.

### Headline (operational narration, per the registered classifier)

**The role header leaks less at the wrong-persona probe but more at the default-assistant probe, under both clean reads.** The frozen classifier returns `concentration_confirmed` — "concentration" is this task's registered operational name for that two-probe pattern, mirroring the Goal; it is **not a mechanism claim**. Scope sentence (binding): the measured 2-probe split does not adjudicate between redistribution/conservation of leakage mass, format-proximity of the default-assistant context to the role-header encoding, or differential effectiveness of the contrastive negatives across arms.

### Finding 1 — The default-assistant excess is unconditional in this grid, and it is the base-prior-clean half

At the default-assistant probe — the only probe whose encoding is identical across arms, so the base prior is identical (−22.09, atol 1e-4) and the cross-arm contrast is base-prior-clean — the role arm carries MORE marker mass at EVERY checkpoint, on BOTH personas, in BOTH spaces: 16 of 16 cells CI-clear in the role-leaks-more direction, with 0/5 positive seeds in 15 cells (1/5 in pirate s120 margin). Villain, where the arms' own-slot implant strengths are matched throughout (within ~1.1 nat in margin space at s≤60), holds a stable excess of ~1.3-1.6 nats at all four checkpoints. This half survives the in-band read (s18, both arms pre-emission), the install-onset read (s30), and the ceiling-free margin read — the parent's average-leakage framing had partially hidden it because the pirate log-p contrast collapses to −0.27 nat at s120 where the margin still reads −1.79 [−2.66, −0.70].

### Finding 2 — The wrong-persona advantage is real from install onward, but absent (and on villain slightly reversed) at the in-band pre-emission point

In margin space at install-onward checkpoints the role arm's wrong-persona advantage is CI-clear on both personas at all of {30, 60, 120}, 5/5 seeds everywhere, growing from ~+0.5 at s30 to ~+3.1 nats (villain s60). But at s18 — the only checkpoint inside the usable band, where own argmax-emit is 0.000 on every arm (in-band but **pre-emission-gate**, NOT "installed off-saturation") — the advantage is ABSENT in log-p space (pirate −0.24 [−0.58, +0.11]; villain −0.02 [−0.19, +0.15]). The classifier's off-saturation verdict is "shrinks": install-coupled, absent at the in-band sub-install point. The advantage is created between s18 and s30, by the install dynamics, not present in the pre-install encoding geometry.

### Finding 3 — The villain s18 margin reversal (a finding in its own right)

At s18 in margin space, villain's wrong-persona contrast is CI-clear in the OPPOSITE direction: d = −0.231 [−0.377, −0.077], 1/5 seeds positive — the minimal SYSTEM prompt leaks slightly less than the role header before the emission gate. The magnitude is small (~0.2 nat against the +0.5 to +3.1 install-onward advantages), but it is not noise by the registered criterion, and it sharpens Finding 2: on villain the pre-install geometry tilts mildly against the role header, and the role advantage that emerges at s30+ is entirely an install-dynamics product. (Log-p space at the same cell straddles: −0.02 [−0.19, +0.15].)

### Finding 4 — Pirate's default slot crosses the emission threshold; the role arm gets there harder (the deployment-relevant number)

The three saturation-flagged cells (pirate-default s30/s60/s120) are exactly where the role-arm pirate model's default-assistant slot approaches the argmax ceiling. At these argmax-adjacent cells — and only here, per the registered scope rule — the excess can be stated in emission terms: at s60/s120 the role-arm pirate model's mean log P(marker) at the default-assistant slot reaches −0.41 / −0.28 (mean per-question probability gain 0.89 / 0.92), i.e. the marker holds the majority of next-token probability at the fixed post-response slot under the bare default-assistant context, vs −1.32 / −0.55 (0.64 / 0.84) for the system arm. Both arms cross the greedy-emission threshold at the default context by s120 on pirate; the role arm crosses earlier and harder. Caveat: this is teacher-forced after BASE-model greedy responses — on-policy default-context responses from the trained model could shift the slot — so it is emission onset at the fixed probe slot, not measured behavioral emission frequency. Everywhere else in the grid, default-slot excess is leakage MASS at a probe slot, not behavior (wrong-persona behavioral emission is 0 across all 4,000 probes of this grid).

### Finding 5 — Honesty check on implant-strength matching (own-slot margin gauge)

The round-1 critique added own-slot Δmargin so cross-arm strength matching could be checked past the log-p ceiling. It shows: villain arms matched throughout (≤1.1 nat apart at s≤60); pirate arms matched in log-p space at s18 (12.12 vs 12.60) but NOT in margin space (12.82 vs 16.74 — role ~3.9 nat latently stronger), with the gap persisting at s30 (25.8 vs 31.4) and INVERTING at s120 (41.1 vs 38.4 — system stronger). Implication: part of the pirate default-half magnitude at s18-s60 may track the role arm's stronger latent implant rather than the encoding per se. Two observations keep the half intact: (i) villain is strength-matched and shows the reversal CI-clear at every checkpoint; (ii) at s120 the reversal holds on both personas while the latent strength gradient points the OTHER way (system stronger). Symmetrically for the wrong half: the s60 advantage runs AGAINST the strength gradient (role latently stronger yet leaks less — the cleanest install-onward read), while the pirate s120 advantage (+1.83) is smaller than system's latent own-slot excess (+2.7) and so is not individually separable from strength there. Magnitudes should be read with this in mind; the directional verdicts do not depend on it.

1. The bare role header's "containment advantage" from #533 is probe-specific: real (and growing with training) at the wrong-persona probe from install onward, but inverted at the default-assistant probe at every checkpoint — and the default-assistant context is the safety-relevant one (leakage-to-default, open-q 3.7).

## Part 2 — Interpretation

### Background

Parent #533's bare-word install-step grid found that a bare `pirate`/`villain` role header carries LESS wrong-persona marker mass than a content-matched minimal system prompt from install onward — but its apparent average-leakage advantage hid a probe split, and the comparison lived partly in a saturated regime where cross-arm log-p contrasts reduce to base-prior differences. This task re-read the parent's committed four-float logit captures with two cleaner measuring sticks: (a) the unsaturated checkpoints (s18 is the only point where both arms sit in/adjacent to the [5, 12]-nat usable band, at matched log-p implant strength, before any emission), and (b) the EOS-margin readout Δ(z_marker − z_eos), which is gauge-invariant and cannot be compressed by the softmax ceiling (valid here because LoRA excludes the unembedding — `gauge_assert.ok` on all 240 cells). Zero new training; the manipulated variable is the readout/regime. The plan's preview (computed during planning over these same files) pointed at the confirmed outcome; the production run re-derived everything from raw arrays with the verdict logic frozen in the plan — this is **disclosed preview-confirmation on the same draws**, not an independent replication.

### Headline (operational narration, per the frozen classifier)

**The role header leaks less at the wrong-persona probe but more at the default-assistant probe, under both clean reads.** The frozen classifier returns `concentration_confirmed` — "concentration" is this task's registered operational name for that two-probe pattern, mirroring the Goal; it is **not a mechanism claim**. Scope sentence (binding): the measured 2-probe split does not adjudicate between redistribution/conservation of leakage mass, format-proximity of the default-assistant context to the role-header encoding, or differential effectiveness of the contrastive negatives across arms.

### Finding 1 — The default-assistant excess is CI-clear at every checkpoint in this grid, and it is the base-prior-clean half

At the default-assistant probe — the only probe whose encoding is identical across arms, so the base prior is identical (−22.09, atol 1e-4) and the cross-arm contrast is base-prior-clean — the role arm carries MORE marker mass at all four checkpoints, on BOTH personas, in BOTH spaces: 16 of 16 cells CI-clear in the role-leaks-more direction, with 0/5 positive seeds in 15 cells (1/5 in pirate s120 margin). Villain, where the arms' own-slot implant strengths are matched throughout (within ~1.1 nat in margin space at s ≤ 60), holds a stable excess of ~1.3-1.6 nats at all four checkpoints with overlapping CIs. Pirate's trajectory is NOT flat: in ceiling-free margin space the excess peaks at s30 (−4.044) and shrinks to −1.793 by s120, with the s30/s120 CIs disjoint and one seed (42) positive at s120 — a real dynamics trend (the system arm catches up late), which tempers any extrapolation beyond s120. The parent's average-leakage framing had partially hidden this half because the pirate log-p contrast collapses to −0.27 nat at s120 where the margin still reads −1.79 [−2.66, −0.70].

### Finding 2 — The wrong-persona advantage appears between s18 and s30 in this grid; it is not detectable at the in-band pre-emission point

In margin space at install-onward checkpoints the role arm's wrong-persona advantage is CI-clear on both personas at all of {30, 60, 120}, 5/5 seeds everywhere, growing from ~+0.5 at s30 to ~+3.1 nats (villain s60). But at s18 — the only checkpoint inside the usable band, where own argmax-emit is 0.000 on every arm (in-band but **pre-emission-gate**, NOT "installed off-saturation") — the advantage is not detectable in log-p space (pirate −0.24 [−0.58, +0.11]; villain −0.02 [−0.19, +0.15]; both CIs straddle). The classifier's off-saturation verdict is "shrinks": install-coupled, absent-by-CI at the in-band sub-install point. Operationally, the advantage appears between s18 and s30 in this grid; with only one sub-install checkpoint, the data do not distinguish WHAT changes in that window (install dynamics vs a threshold/regime-timing effect), so no mechanism is claimed. One residual caveat on this half: the wrong-persona d compares Δ's computed over different probe texts across arms (arm-specific encodings) — the base-Δ differencing controls the base level, not base × training interactions.

### Finding 3 — The villain s18 margin reversal (a finding in its own right)

At s18 in margin space, villain's wrong-persona contrast is CI-clear in the OPPOSITE direction: d = −0.231 [−0.377, −0.077], 1/5 seeds positive — the minimal SYSTEM prompt leaks slightly less than the role header before the emission gate. The magnitude is small (~0.2 nat against the +0.5 to +3.1 install-onward advantages), but it is not noise by the plan-frozen criterion, and it sharpens Finding 2: on villain the pre-emission contrast tilts mildly against the role header, and the role advantage measured from s30 onward emerges between s18 and s30. (Log-p space at the same cell straddles: −0.02 [−0.19, +0.15].)

### Finding 4 — Pirate's default slot crosses the emission threshold by s60; the role arm gets there harder (the deployment-relevant number)

Two distinct cell classes need separating here (round-1 critique). **Saturation-compressed** (the |d_logp − d_margin| flag): pirate-default s30, s60, AND s120 — at all three the margin is authoritative. **Argmax-adjacent emission onset** (the plan's criterion: role-arm trained log P at or above −0.55): only s60 and s120. At s30 the role-arm pirate default slot reads trained log P −3.635 — compressed but NOT emission-adjacent, so its excess stays narrated as leakage mass. At s60/s120 the role-arm pirate model's mean log P(marker) at the default-assistant slot reaches −0.41 / −0.28 (mean per-question probability gain 0.89 / 0.92): the marker holds the majority of next-token probability at the fixed post-response slot under the bare default-assistant context on 90% / 94% of the 50 probe questions (5-seed mean fractions with trained P above 0.5), vs −1.32 / −0.55 (0.64 / 0.84; majority fractions 68% / 84%) for the system arm. Both arms put the marker past the greedy-emission threshold at the probe slot on most questions by s120 on pirate; the role arm crosses earlier and harder. Caveat: this is teacher-forced after BASE-model greedy responses — on-policy default-context responses from the trained model could shift the slot — so it is emission onset at the fixed probe slot, not measured behavioral emission frequency. Everywhere else in the grid, default-slot excess is leakage MASS at a probe slot, not behavior (wrong-persona behavioral emission is 0 across all 4,000 probes of this grid).

### Finding 5 — Honesty check on implant-strength matching (own-slot margin gauge)

The round-1 plan critique added own-slot Δmargin so cross-arm strength matching could be checked past the log-p ceiling. It shows: villain arms matched throughout (≤1.1 nat apart at s ≤ 60); pirate arms matched in log-p space at s18 (12.12 vs 12.60) but NOT in margin space (12.82 vs 16.74 — role ~3.9 nat latently stronger), with the gap at s30 widening to ~5.6 nat (25.8 vs 31.4), shrinking to ~1.4 nat at s60 (37.85 vs 39.29), and INVERTING at s120 (41.1 vs 38.4 — system ~2.7 nat stronger). Implication: part of the pirate default-half magnitude at s18-s30 may track the role arm's stronger latent implant rather than the encoding per se — and the latent-gap trajectory (peak ~5.6 at s30, inversion by s120) loosely parallels the non-monotonic pirate default-half excess (peak −4.04 at s30, shrink to −1.79 at s120), consistent with strength entanglement driving part of the pirate magnitude. Two observations keep the half intact: (i) villain is strength-matched and shows the reversal CI-clear at every checkpoint; (ii) at s120 the reversal holds on both personas while the latent strength gradient points the OTHER way (system stronger). Symmetrically for the wrong half: the s60 advantage runs AGAINST the strength gradient (role latently stronger yet leaks less — the cleanest install-onward read), while the pirate s120 advantage (+1.83) is smaller than system's latent own-slot excess (~2.7) and so is not individually separable from strength there. Magnitudes should be read with this in mind; the directional verdicts do not depend on it.

### Main takeaways

1. The bare role header's "containment advantage" from #533 is probe-specific: real (and growing with training) at the wrong-persona probe from install onward, but inverted at the default-assistant probe at every checkpoint in this grid — and the default-assistant context is the safety-relevant one (leakage-to-default, open-q 3.7).
2. The default-half excess is the better-measured half: encoding-identical base prior, 16/16 CI-clear cells, robust to the ceiling-free margin read, and on the strength-matched persona (villain) it is stable at ~1.3-1.6 nats. On pirate it is non-monotonic — peaks at s30, shrinks by s120 (CIs disjoint) — so it should not be extrapolated past s120.
3. The wrong-persona advantage is not detectable at the in-band pre-emission point (s18) — on villain it points slightly the other way in margin space — and appears between s18 and s30 in this grid. With one sub-install checkpoint, the data do not say what changes in that window.
4. Saturated log-p cells understate real contrasts by up to ~6x (pirate default s120: −0.27 log-p vs −1.79 margin); the four-float capture + margin readout is what made this split readable at all.
5. Operationally: relative to the minimal system prompt, choosing the bare role header to contain the implant buys lower wrong-persona probe mass at the cost of HIGHER default-assistant probe mass at every checkpoint — by s60+ on pirate, past the greedy-emission threshold at the probe slot. Whether total leakage mass is globally redistributed or removed is not measured by this two-probe rig.

### Confidence: MODERATE

**Why confidence is where it is.** Supporting: the default half is base-prior-clean by construction, CI-clear in 16/16 cells with near-unanimous seed signs, agrees across both readout spaces (and where they disagree, the flagged cells, the margin holds the sign), and the verdict logic was frozen in the approved plan before the production run. Capping at MODERATE: (i) this is a re-read of the SAME eval draws the planning preview already examined — disclosed preview-confirmation, not independent replication on new data; (ii) the DV is a teacher-forced fixed-slot proxy after base-greedy responses (the only readout with dynamic range here — wrong-persona behavioral emission is 0 in all 4,000 probes), so "leaks more/less" means leakage mass at the probe slot, not measured behavior, except at the argmax-adjacent pirate default cells (s60/s120) where emission onset at the slot is explicit; (iii) n = 2 personas with a visible pirate/villain asymmetry — per-persona verdicts are never pooled, and generality beyond these two personas is untested; (iv) the own-slot margin gauge shows the pirate arms were not strength-matched at s18-s60, so the pirate default-half MAGNITUDE is partly entangled with implant strength (direction is protected by villain + the s120 against-gradient read), and the pirate excess itself shrinks late (s30 vs s120 CIs disjoint).
